project.title: DP-PFN: Differentially Private Prior-Data Fitted Networks
project.domain: differential privacy / prior-data fitted networks / machine learning

question.text: How can prior-data fitted networks (TabPFN, NodePFN) be used for differentially private tabular and graph prediction so that weights cost no privacy budget, while certificates come from black-box wrappers or noise-aware post-processing rather than from training loss?

hypotheses.text: If PFN weights are trained only on synthetic prior data and preprocessing is shard-local or public, privacy accounting reduces to the context release. A black-box Vote/LogPool/Student wrapper, or a noise-aware reader of an already-private summary S=M(D), is (ε,δ)-DP regardless of approximation error (Prop. 0, Cor. B4, Thm. D1).
hypotheses.evidence: Prop. 0 and the wrapper/post-processing guarantees are correct (X0). Must add a third route: certified-by-architecture PFNs (PrivTab, arXiv 2610.10068). TREDBench caveat: synthetic-task selection uses real data.

hypotheses.text: No bound on PFN training loss certifies worst-case DP (Prop. B2). On closed-form floored priors, the log-gap Λ(D) and row-sensitivity s(θ,n) stay small on prior-typical datasets but can be driven large on adversarial neighbouring pairs; a more accurate PFN leaks more unless the training target itself is private (Obs. B5).
hypotheses.evidence: E1-lite: Lambda small on typical data and larger adversarially (supported); network leakage exceeds the exact mechanism's worst case by up to ~2.5x in support (supported: exact-PPD privacy is not inherited); but leakage stayed below 2B_y everywhere searched (the 'driven large' part not observed for a small LayerNorm network); better-trained PFNs leak more (Obs. B5 supported).

hypotheses.text: At fixed ε, DP-PFN-Vote sample size n* is set by teacher error e(m) at small shard size m (Thm. C2). A PFN teacher therefore attains a smaller n* than per-shard trained PATE teachers, and the minimizing m matches the C2 prediction.
hypotheses.source: proposal Section 4; tested by E2, E3
hypotheses.evidence: E3-lite (idealised Gaussian prior, exact-Bayes teacher): PFN-like teachers lower DP-Vote error at small n*eps, and C2 picks m within 2x. But C2 must be pointwise (bias floor 13-16% at m=2) and its n* is conservative by ~3-10x. Real PFN teachers and tuned/charged trained teachers still to test (E2/E3).

hypotheses.text: A PFN trained with the release mechanism inside the prior matches the private-data posterior predictive. Versus naive TabPFN on the same release, it reduces under-confidence on label randomized response and over-confidence on bulk DP synthetic rows, lowering NLL and ECE at the same ε (Thm. D1, Prop. D2).
hypotheses.source: proposal Section 5; tested by E4, Gate 2
hypotheses.evidence: Label RR: D2-check (exact targets) plus E4-lite (trained network) recover most of the calibration gain at equal accuracy. Synthetic half: D2-sparse (512 cells, exact targets) finds naive use under-confident in 8 of 9 cells, growing with n, so the predicted over-confidence does not survive sparsity. The noise-aware target still lowers NLL in every cell. Open: real data and TabPFN scale, and generators that preserve margins exactly.

history.text: Proposal read end-to-end (25 pages). Hypotheses H1–H4 registered from Sections 1–5. No experiment has been run; E1–E8 remain planned. Background citations in the PDF were not re-checked by the authors.

Plan reviewed: theory audit (X0), citation audit + related work (PrivTab, Private PoEtry, TabPATE overlap), and four CPU pilots (E1-lite, E3-lite, D2-check, G3-check). See reviews/2026-11-05-plan-review.md.
Independent rerun on a second machine (gpu-gfkd; commit 8f95ca4 logs) reproduced E1 training exactly and E1/E3/D2/G3 numbers within sampling noise.

E4-lite: A trained noise-aware PFN on label-RR releases recovers 71-86% of the exact noise-aware NLL gain over naive plug-in at n=128 (NLL 0.623/0.575/0.554 vs naive 0.644/0.604/0.565), with unchanged accuracy and no cost on clean data (max NLL difference 0.0002). The naive PFN matches the exact naive target (KL <= 0.0013), i.e. it is under-confident as Prop. D2 predicts. Gate 2: pass (pilot, label RR only).

experiments.title: Numerical audit of all proposal constants; exact one-draw privacy loss
experiments.summary: All constants reproduce. Thm A2 tight for the posterior draw (2.193 vs 2B_y=2.197 at n=1000); the clean-target release (A5) costs ~B_y, half the bound; a noisy-PPD label costs 0.0034 at n=1000. Prop. G3 threshold for the worked example is 290 (dense SNR), not 311.

experiments.title: Exact vs amortized privacy loss of a small PFN on a floored logistic prior
experiments.summary: Trained PFN (excess NLL 0.0006 over exact Bayes): on prior-typical data its label-DP leakage tracks the exact PPD's (median ratio 0.84-1.42; gap Lambda median <= 0.21). Gradient search finds in-support neighbours where it leaks 1.2-2.5x the exact mechanism's worst case, and the gap grows out of support (Lambda up to 2.24). Largest leakage found 1.79, below 2B_y in every setting. An under-trained checkpoint leaks 0.10-1.40x the exact level (Obs. B5).

experiments.title: Theorem C2 vs simulation; Bayes vs trained teachers; Vote vs LogPool
experiments.summary: Exact-Bayes (PFN-like) teachers beat trained logistic-regression teachers under DP-Vote by +4.1/+3.7/+2.3 points at eps=0.1 (n=250/500/1000); the gap vanishes at large n*eps. Even Bayes teachers leave a 13-16% infinite-T error floor at m=2, so C2 must be pointwise. C2 argmax m is within 2x of the observed best in 42/45 configs, but its n* (1,176-5,077) is very conservative. LogPool loses to Vote by up to 7.5 points with calibrated teachers.

experiments.title: Naive vs noise-aware use of label-RR and DP synthetic data (exact Bayes)
experiments.summary: Label RR: naive is under-confident, growing with n (n=1000, eps=0.5: ECE 0.165 vs 0.068, over-confidence -0.159 vs -0.001); noise-aware fixes it at equal accuracy. DP synthetic data: naive over-confident only at n=50 (+0.032) in a 2-parameter model.

experiments.title: Trained noise-aware PFN vs naive PFN on label-RR releases
experiments.summary: A trained noise-aware PFN on label-RR releases recovers 71-86% of the exact noise-aware NLL gain over naive plug-in at n=128 (NLL 0.623/0.575/0.554 vs naive 0.644/0.604/0.565), with unchanged accuracy and no cost on clean data (max NLL difference 0.0002). The naive PFN matches the exact naive target (KL <= 0.0013), i.e. it is under-confident as Prop. D2 predicts.

experiments.title: Spectral recovery on edge-RR SBMs vs threshold formulas
experiments.summary: Simulation follows the dense spiked-matrix SNR (variance p'(1-p')); thresholds 59/290/2739 at eps=1/2/4. At N=1024, eps=2 structural signal is gone (overlap 0.04).
